function: Learned joint UAV placement, DFT-codebook beam selection, transmit power control and RB allocation for UAV base stations serving eMBB and URLLC users (p. 3).
system: 4 UAVs with 8 antennas each serve 24 eMBB and 8 URLLC single-antenna ground UEs, downlink, 32 RBs, 1.9 GHz, no RIS (p. 2, Table II p. 4).
method: Attention-enhanced MAPPO: four heterogeneous MLP actor-critic agents per UAV (2x256), centralized training with distributed execution, trained by multi-agent reinforcement learning (p. 3-4).
data_channel: Own simulator, no dataset: LoS plus Rician fading, Rician factor 10^(1.3-0.003d), path loss -36.7log10(d)-22.7-26log10(f), 4 dB shadowing; random UE positions; online training (p. 2, p. 4).
test_conditions: 1,000 training episodes of 10 steps, UE QoS requirements random per episode; learning curves and converged values in one Table II setup, no new scenario (p. 4-5).
baselines: Learned: MAPPO, MATD3, MADQN (p. 5). Partial-resource variants of the proposed scheme: BFRA, DP-BF, BF (p. 4). No non-learned method compared.
metrics: System utility (economic profit), profit, cost, and QoS satisfaction ratio (p. 4-5).
complexity: Training O(4MBE Tep (La+Lc)(An^2+Ac^2)); execution O(4M La An^2), analytical orders only, no runtime (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 2: "channel model with line-of-sight (LoS) path and Rician distributed small-scale fading"; custom simulator, no standardized model or measured data named (path loss cites [5], p. 4).
q2_support: p. 4: "We consider a dynamic scenario, where the UEs' QoS requirements vary randomly across episodes." This is training-time variation; results are learning curves in the single Table II configuration, with no test in a new scenario.
q3_support: p. 5: "multi-agent twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (MATD3) [17]" and MAPPO, MADQN are learned baselines; BFRA, DP-BF, BF (p. 4) are partial variants of the proposed MA-DRL, so no non-learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 4: "the complexity of the MADRL algorithm can be represented as O(4MBETep (La + Lc)(A2n + A2c ))" and "decision-making complexity of O(4MLa A2n)".
q5_support: p. 4: "32 ground UEs are randomly distributed in this area"; data come from the authors' own simulator, and the paper gives no code or data link or DOI and uses no public dataset.
notes: Included as area 6: learned beam selection, power control and RB allocation on aerial links are physical layer (p. 3), learned jointly with UAV placement, so the above_phy check passes. Area 6 wins over 3 by the specificity order. q3 fails only for the missing non-learned baseline. The paper does not name 3GPP for its path loss (p. 4).
